shared_inputs.notes: Ensures orders data is loaded so custkey_to_orders grouped_fk index is usable for NOT EXISTS check
Iterate all 1.5M customer rows for scalar subquery and main filter+aggregate pass

operators.description: Compute AVG(c_acctbal) over customer WHERE c_acctbal > 0.00 AND SUBSTRING(c_phone,1,2) IN ('13','31','23','29','30','18','17')
operators.notes: Single sequential pass over 1.5M customer rows. Extract first 2 chars of c_phone varlen, check membership in 7-element set (use lookup table or small hash). Accumulate sum and count, divide at end.

operators.description: For each qualifying customer, check NOT EXISTS in orders using custkey_to_orders grouped_fk index
operators.notes: Second pass over 1.5M customer rows. Apply phone prefix filter first (28% selectivity), then c_acctbal > avg (50% selectivity), then anti-join via custkey_to_orders index O(1) lookup (~30% of remaining survive). This avoids scanning 15M orders rows entirely.

operators.description: GROUP BY cntrycode (SUBSTRING(c_phone,1,2)), compute COUNT(*) and SUM(c_acctbal)
operators.notes: Fuse aggregation into the step 2 loop. Map each 2-char phone prefix to bucket index 0-6 via small lookup table. Each bucket holds {count: int64, sum: double}. Only 7 groups so no hash table needed — direct array of 112 bytes total.
7 rows — just sort bucket array by country code string. Essentially free.

indexes.notes: Only offsets array needed — check offsets[custkey+1] == offsets[custkey] for NOT EXISTS. rows array not accessed.
Customer has dense_pk with max_key=1500000, enabling iteration over all rows by index 0..1499999

data_structures.phone_prefix_lookup: fixed_array[100] mapping 2-digit int to bucket_id (0-6) or -1, populated at init from set {'13','17','18','23','29','30','31'}
data_structures.scalar_accumulator: struct { double sum; int64_t count; } for AVG computation in step 1
data_structures.agg_buckets: array[7] of struct { int64_t count; double sum; } — 112 bytes total, fits in L1 cache

parallelism.notes: Customer is only 1.5M rows with varlen c_phone access. Two lightweight sequential passes (avg computation, then filter+anti-join+aggregate) complete in ~10-20ms each. Parallelism overhead would exceed savings. The custkey_to_orders index lookup is random access but fits in memory. Total work is dominated by c_phone varlen decoding.

execution_notes.phone_prefix_extraction: Read first 2 bytes of c_phone varlen string, convert to 2-digit integer (e.g., '13' -> 13), use as index into phone_prefix_lookup array
execution_notes.scan_orders_dependency: scan_orders_full must complete before step 2 to ensure custkey_to_orders index offsets are valid in memory. However, step 1 (avg computation) can begin as soon as hash_customer_by_custkey is ready.
execution_notes.memory_estimate: custkey_to_orders offsets array: ~6MB (1.5M+1 int32 entries). Customer columns (c_phone, c_acctbal): already loaded by shared component. Working memory: <1KB for accumulators.
